C. Every mode: the fields it uses and where it lands

• The director accepts one packet a cycle and routes it by mode alone, and never stalls: an overflow of the write-engine input FIFO sets condition 2. Port B has no other writer.

• Read-port results share the tile's loopback and eject path with every arriving packet, and the network has no flow control, so no packet from outside the tile, other than C&C's mode-6 command words, may
arrive while read-port results are outstanding (§4.3, invariant 14). The hardware tolerates only 15 results against a full-rate stream, or 32 per burst at half rate [meas: meshsim].

• Programming errors with no hardware check (the simulator checks them): a mode-5 address outside both memories (invariant 11); a mode-7 address in the mailbox or outside data memory (invariants 12, 13);
• The packed 12-bit map (mode 5's addresses, and mode 7's as SRAM_RD_DEST_ADDR writes them, §4.3) and the mailbox at 0x5C00–0x5FFF (data words 0x700–0x7FF).
one per cycle; the director never stalls
port B: addr, wdata, we[1:0], memory
counted packets (src ≠ 64); a mode-6 write to slot 0
Every packet is routed by its 4-bit mode: mode 1 to the GATHER engine, 2–4 to the write engine (which forms the address from PTR), 5–7 to port B
(which forms memory, word and banks from addr); 0 and 8–15 are dropped with the bad-mode condition. Read-port results are mode-7 packets. Counting happens on acceptance.
